metadata.methods_description: Intracranial electrophysiological recordings were collected during a spatial navigation memory task consisting of learning and test phases. Learning trials involved participants being placed at random locations and automatically driven to object locations, while test trials required self-navigation to remembered object locations. Recordings were acquired using Blackrock and Medtronic systems across multiple clinical sites. Monopolar recordings were referenced (typically mastoid) and bipolar recordings followed paired electrode schemes. MNI and Talairach coordinates are provided for electrode locations.

citation_details.title: Spatial Memory of Object Locations with Open-Loop Stimulation at Encoding
citation_details.author: Haydn Herrema, Michael J. Kahana
citation_details.abstract: This dataset contains intracranial electrophysiological recordings and behavioral data from a spatial navigation memory task with open-loop brain stimulation during encoding. Participants learned object locations through guided navigation and subsequently recalled them during self-navigation test phases. The study employed electrical stimulation of hippocampal and entorhinal cortex electrodes during learning trials, with stimulation parameters systematically varied across counterbalanced trial blocks to investigate the effects of targeted brain stimulation on spatial memory encoding. This dataset is an open-loop stimulation variant of the YC1 dataset (ds005522).
